posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
I am not so interested in buying film that will go out of stock. I you want to buy in large quantities, perhaps Filmotec material is much more interesting. They have a green sensitive film that costs about 160 Euro for 5 sheets of 50x60cm. That comes to less than 2 Euro per sheet of 10x15cm. 

The resulotion for the fast film is >3000 lines/mm and the speed is 250uJ at 532nm. They also have a high resolution film that has >5000L/mm for the same price. The highest resolution film has 1000uJ sensitivity.

Here is the link: [http://www.filmotec.de](http://www.filmotec.de)

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **Hans:** I am not so interested in buying film that will go out of stock.

Do you mean you don't want to become dependent on a film that will no longer be available at some point in the future?

That could happen with any of our films. It's a really small market.

If we can get enough of a discount, we could probably buy enough stock to last a while, assuming they have quantity available.

The price on the filmotec is good but the sensitivity really stinks. It requires almost 4x the exposure as VRPM and more than 2x PFG01.

It looks like several people on the forum have tried the film but nobody's shared the results.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
I did try the GF-40 once for DCG. That is a gelatin only film. I got the brightest hologram I ever made. I found that the problem with the GF-40 was that the base was very thin: 125um. The GF-55 comes in a thickness of 190um. That should make it somewhat easier to index match it flat.

For the sensitivity issue. You are right. But the basic specification is about the same as that for Fuji: 250uJ for Filmotec versus 200uJ for Fuji. I found that I could get away with exposures of 70uJ on Fuji for transmission work. Perhaps the same goes for Filmotec. Kris Meerloo will send me a sample package that he still has in his fridge. I will test it next week and let you know how it goes.
